name: GPO Misconfiguration Abuse (SharpGPOAbuse)
description: Identify and abuse write access to Group Policy Objects to execute arbitrary code on all computers in the affected OU.

examples.label: Find GPOs where we have write access
Add machine scheduled task
examples.command: .\SharpGPOAbuse.exe --AddComputerTask --TaskName 'Updater' --Author 'NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM' --Command 'cmd.exe' --Arguments '/c net localgroup administrators jdoe /add' --GPOName 'Default Domain Policy'

recommended.note: Dump creds once local admin via GPO
ACL persistence for more targeted abuse

notes: GPO write access = code execution on every computer the GPO applies to. Very powerful. Requires gpupdate cycle for task to execute.

defense.why_it_works: Group Policy Objects control system configuration across the domain. If a non-admin account has write permissions on a GPO (CreateChild, WriteProperty, or GenericWrite via BloodHound ACL analysis), SharpGPOAbuse can modify that GPO to add a local admin, schedule a task, or set a registry run key — affecting all computers and users in the linked OU. Changes take effect at the next Group Policy refresh (90 min default, or gpupdate /force).
defense.prerequisites: Write permissions on a GPO (identified via BloodHound: 'Find GPOs where Domain Users have Modify Rights'). SharpGPOAbuse or PowerGPOAbuse. Domain user account. The GPO must be linked to an OU containing target computers/users.
defense.impact: T1484.001 Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification. Code execution on all computers in the linked OU. Local admin rights on targeted systems. Persistent via GPO — survives reboots. Can add a scheduled task that runs on all workstations in the domain if linked at domain level.
defense.detection:
Event 5136 on the GPO object: DACL or GPO content modified. Event 5145: GPO file accessed from SYSVOL share. SIEM: GPO content changes from non-admin source. Windows Event 4728 (group member added) if GPO adds local admin. Sysmon Event 11: file write to SYSVOL\{GUID}\Machine\Microsoft\Windows NT\SecEdit\. MDI: GPO modification alert.
Adversary modifies GPOs, domain trust, or directory service objects via GUI, CLI, or programmatic APIs: creation/modification of GPOs, delegation permissions, trust objects, or rogue DC registration (DET0270/AN0755). Adversary modifies tenant policy through changes to federation configuration, trust settings, or identity provider additions in Microsoft 365/Azure AD via Portal, PowerShell, or Graph API; includes setting authentication to federated or updating federated domains (AN0756).
defense.artifacts: Event 5136: GPO object modified | SYSVOL file change: GptTmpl.inf or {GUID}.xml written by non-admin | Event 4728: unexpected local admin group addition on target hosts | Sysmon: SYSVOL write from workstation | MDI: GPO modification alert
defense.prevention:
Audit GPO DACLs with BloodHound: 'Find GPOs where Domain Users have Modify Rights'. Remove non-admin write permissions on GPOs. Enable GPMC logging. Monitor Event 5136 on GPO objects. Require change control for GPO modifications (only via dedicated GPO management workstation). MDI deployment.
Audit: Identify and correct GPO permissions abuse opportunities using auditing tools such as BloodHound.
Privileged Account Management: Use least privilege; protect administrative access to Domain Controllers and AD FS servers; do not create service accounts with administrative privileges.
User Account Management: Implement WMI and security filtering to tailor which users and computers a GPO applies to.
defense.evasion: Modify GPO to add a scheduled task that runs at startup/login (blends with legitimate GPO startup scripts). Use an existing GPO that's already applied rather than creating a new one. GPO changes have 90-min delay — makes correlation harder.
defense.misconfiguration: Non-admin groups have write permissions on GPOs (often from legacy delegation or mis-scoped admin roles). No Event 5136 monitoring on GPO objects. GPO DACLs not regularly audited.
defense.secure_config:
# Remove non-admin write ACEs from GPOs:
# GPMC → right-click GPO → Edit Delegations → remove non-admin edit rights

# Audit GPO DACLs with BloodHound:
# Cypher: MATCH (g:GPO) WHERE g.owned=true RETURN g.name
# Or: 'Find GPOs where Domain Users have Modify Rights' built-in query

# Enable Event 5136 on GPO objects:
# Advanced Audit: DS Access → Audit Directory Service Changes
# SIEM: EventID=5136 AND ObjectDN contains 'CN=Policies,CN=System' → ALERT

# Change control: require ITSM ticket for GPO modifications
# Only GPO admins (dedicated group) have write rights — review quarterly

variations.label: Abuse via GPOddity (Linux/WSL, lab method)
